correctness.rationale: The symmetric Skellam law and telescoping Bessel recurrence give \(\mathbb ER=t e^{-t}(I_0(t)+I_1(t))\) and \(\mathbb ER^2=t\). Hence \(\operatorname{Var}(R)-\mathbb ER=t(1-H(t))\). The strict classical Turán inequality orders positive Bessel ratios and, through the generating series, yields \(r>1-I_1/I_0\). At each positive zero of \(H-1\), \(H\prime =r^2(1-r-u)/((1-r)(1+u))<0\), where \(u=I_1/I_0\). As \(t\downarrow0\) the difference \(H-1\) is positive, whereas as \(t\to\infty\) it tends to \(2/\pi-1<0\). Therefore every zero is a strict downward crossing and exactly one zero exists. Exact rational tail-bounded certificates prove \(3.4778<t_*<3.4780\). The independent finite Poisson-sum moments agreed with the Bessel expression at four intensities; they do not prove the all-real theorem.

originality.rationale: The article on Poisson order statistics establishes underdispersion of the individual extrema, not their range. Folded-Skellam application literature uses the count difference as a distribution, not the unique sign change of Var(range)-E(range). Classical Bessel inequalities are prerequisites but not the transition theorem. Related exact moment identities, maximum-versus-parent-variance crossings, and Fano orderings do not imply a single range-versus-own-mean crossing without the new inequality and zero-crossing proof. Completed public and mathematical-record searches identified no exact or dominating theorem. Residual access gaps and unknown earlier literature remain explicit.

value.rationale: The absolute Poisson count difference is a natural imbalance/range statistic directly used in folded Skellam models. This theorem finds and proves the unique point at which its variance crosses its own mean, clarifying a counterintuitive failure of individual Poisson-order-statistic underdispersion under taking their difference. The number is not an arbitrary slice: it is the unique natural Fano-index phase boundary. The strict inequality controlling all crossings is structural and supports future dispersion diagnostics; a mere numerical bracket is not the contribution.
